newsitem.title: UK: IMF, Bulgaria in focus for emerging market traders.
newsitem.headline: IMF, Bulgaria in focus for emerging market traders.

text.p: With the IMF meeting in Washington and a number of developing countries readying new debt issues, emerging market investors will have plenty to chew on in the week ahead.

Investors will be watching the annual meeting of the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank for word on whether BULGARIA has won a much delayed second tranche of an IMF loan, crucial to haul the country out of economic crisis.
"Everyone wants to know whether Bulgaria will get the IMF loan," said Paul Luke, head of emerging market research at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
"Bulgaria wants endorsement from (IMF chief Michel) Camdessus to stop the currency's collapse," he added.
Last week Bulgaria jacked up interest rates to a record 300 percent to halt the run on the lev, which had plummeted to 230 to the dollar from 70 in January.
The rate rise, and Sofia's decision to speed up its privatisation process, were designed to convince the IMF to release the promised $115 million tranche and restore confidence in the ailing economy.
Investors will also be looking for any signs that ECUADOR will approach the IMF for financial help.
"It may be their turn next," said Deutsche Morgan Grenfell's Luke. "They may approach the IMF next week."
Investors expect the IMF to release the September tranche of RUSSIA's $10 billion three-year loan, which is subject to tough monthly monitoring, after discussions with the IMF this week.

While Russian President Boris Yeltsin prepares to undergo a heart by-pass operation in six to eight weeks' time, investors are hoping for news of the country's projected credit rating. Many are increasingly anticipating an investment grade cachet.
BRAZIL will dominate market headlines out of Latin America as local elections get underway on October 3.

"It seems the slight rally in favour of (President Fernando Henrique) Cardoso has petered out and (his party) is looking at 19 percent of the poll," one debt market analyst said, but added the swing has already been priced into the debt market.

Brazil is rumoured to be preparing a $750 million five or 10 year global issue for possible launch this week, and Argentina may weigh in with a $750 million 10-year bond at around 400-425 basis points over Treasuries.
News of the Argentine deal boosted its Bradys on Friday.

After violence engulfed the West Bank last week and ISRAEL declared a state of emergency, edgy investors will be eyeing their portfolios. The benchmark Mishtanim index of 100 top shares lost 4.0 percent in one day last week.
Politicking will being in earnest in THAILAND this week after Prime Minister Banharn Silpa-archa on Friday called elections for November 17.

State Bank of INDIA takes its roadshow for a $400 million Global depositary receipt to the United States. Analysts say the issue looks likely to be well received despite the background of political troubles which have embroiled Prime Minister P.V. Narasimha Rao.
On Friday the IFC's benchmark composite index of emergingpercent week on week at 297.39 points.
Latin America was off 0.9 percent over the week at 536.05, Asia was off 0.1 percent at 252.62, and Europe, Middle East and Africa was down 1.1 percent at 140.59.
